sections.title: Market Pulse: US Equities Decline Amid Rising Oil Prices and Treasury Yields

items.headline: US stocks opened lower today, driven by surging crude oil prices and multi-year high Treasury yields. Investors are reacting to President Trump's rejection of an Iranian proposal, which has exacerbated geopolitical tensions and inflation concerns.
items.summary: Major indices experienced declines in early trading, reversing some of the robust performance from the previous week. The economic landscape remains pressured by elevated energy costs and a hawkish Federal Reserve outlook, with key inflation and jobs data anticipated later in the week.

items.headline: Atlas Energy Solutions Surges
items.summary: Atlas Energy Solutions ($AESI) led market gainers today, climbing +13.5%.

items.headline: Kodiak Sciences Jumps Ahead of Study Results
items.summary: Kodiak Sciences ($KOD) saw shares rise +7% ahead of its planned release of topline results for the DAYBREAK Phase 3 study evaluating treatments for wet age-related macular degeneration.

items.headline: Nvidia Boosted by Expanded Buyback Program
items.summary: Nvidia ($NVDA) shares rose +2% after its board increased the share repurchase authorization by $150 billion, bringing the total remaining authorization to $235 billion. This expanded program is reportedly the largest buyback authorization in U.S. history and is fueled by strong cash generation from AI demand.

items.headline: NIO Shares Climb on Strategic Stake Acquisition
items.summary: NIO ($NIO) shares increased by +2% following Zhejiang Geely Holding Group's agreement to acquire a 30% stake in NIO's battery-swapping business.

items.headline: Inflation Risks Escalate, Fed Considers Further Rate Hikes
items.summary: Fed Governor Michael Barr indicated that inflation risks have intensified, suggesting further discussions around interest rate increases may be necessary. US swap markets are pricing in one to two additional rate hikes by year-end, following the Fed's recent tightening path. The Fed is also reportedly preparing to revise asset thresholds for banks to reflect inflation and economic growth.

items.headline: Oil Prices Surge as US Rejects Iran Proposal
items.summary: Crude oil prices saw a significant rise today, with WTI futures trading around $95.57 per barrel and Brent crude around $106.02 per barrel. This surge follows President Trump's rejection of an Iranian proposal to end the conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, intensifying geopolitical uncertainty.

items.headline: Micron and Jefferies Among Companies Reporting Earnings This Week
items.summary: Micron is scheduled to release its earnings report on Wednesday, while Jefferies Financial Group ($JEF) is expected to post its quarterly earnings of 93 cents per share on revenue of $2.17 billion after the closing bell today. Investors will be closely watching these reports for insights into corporate performance.

items.headline: Treasury Yields Hit Multi-Decade Highs
items.summary: The 10-year US Treasury yield climbed above 5.2% today, reaching its highest level since mid-2007. The 2-year yield also reached its highest point since May 2024. These elevated yields are impacting equity markets and reflecting expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening.

items.headline: Communication Services Led Gains on Friday, Materials and Utilities Lagged
items.summary: On Friday, the Communication Services Select Sector SPDR ($XLC) rose by 1.3%, leading eight out of eleven sectors of the S&P 500 into positive territory. Conversely, the Materials Select Sector SPDR ($XLB) fell 1.2% and the Utilities Select Sector SPDR ($XLU) dropped 1%, making them among the lagging sectors.
